Gold just fell nineteen thousand rupees in nine trading days. Could you have known before your jeweller changed the price? Almost. But that's not prediction.
India imports almost all its gold. So the price is not made here. It starts in America, on Comex, in dollars per ounce.
And Comex trades while India sleeps. By the time our market opens at nine in the morning, the night's move is already done.
Here's the formula. Take the Comex price, multiply by the rupee rate, divide by three point one one for ten grams, and add fifteen percent import duty.

Real check. On November eighteenth, spot gold was three thousand seven hundred ninety seven dollars, and the rupee was ninety three point four four. The formula says one lakh thirty one thousand. M C X opened at one lakh thirty one thousand six hundred.
This morning, gold fell overnight, so M C X opened three percent lower. Your jeweller's rate is built on the same numbers, plus three percent G S T and making charges.
But that only tells you the next morning. Nobody knows next month. The US Fed, the dollar, wars and central banks move it every night.
And the government can move it overnight too. In May this year, gold import duty jumped from six to fifteen percent.
So watch Comex and the rupee to know early. Don't bet on predictions. Save this formula, and follow money in cloud.
